name: peanut butter
answer: Yes, as a normal spread. Dietitians who follow Monash's lab results list 2 tablespoons (50 g) of plain peanut butter as low FODMAP, or 32 g for the American-style kind. Choose a jar made from just peanuts and salt.

servings.note: From dietitian sites reporting Monash's lab results; not on Monash's or FODMAP Friendly's own sites. No upper limit is currently published.
From dietitian sites reporting Monash's lab results; not on Monash's or FODMAP Friendly's own sites.

changes.text: George Eats reports that Monash used to list 140 g of peanut butter as moderate, and has since removed that upper limit while it updates its data.

disagreements.text: George Eats reports that FODMAP Friendly rates peanut butter low up to 167 g, far above Monash's two-tablespoon serve.
Both Monash entries are '2 tablespoons' but weigh 50 g and 32 g. The sources don't explain the gap, so weighing is more reliable than a spoon.

notes.text: Monash's low FODMAP shopping list names peanut butter among its spreads.
George Eats suggests a peanut butter whose only ingredients are peanuts and salt.

swaps.name: Almond butter, in a smaller spoon

faq.q: Is crunchy peanut butter low FODMAP?
faq.a: The sources don't split smooth from crunchy. Read the label for added sweeteners or fibres and keep to the usual two-tablespoon spread.

name: almonds
answer: Yes, in a small handful. Monash lists 10 almonds (12 g) as a low FODMAP serve. Dietitian sites that track Monash's newer data put the limit nearer 22 to 24 g, with GOS turning moderate from 25 g, so a big handful is where it adds up.

servings.note: The 12 g serve is Monash's own (2021). The moderate amount comes from George Eats, reporting Monash's current data.

changes.text: George Eats reports that Monash now lists almonds as low up to about 22 to 24 g (around 20 nuts), roughly double the older 10-nut serve.

disagreements.text: George Eats gives 22 g on its nut list and 24 g on its almond page. Both say GOS becomes moderate at 25 g.
Older guides based on earlier Monash data treated 20 almonds as a moderate serve.

notes.text: Monash's Step 1 sheet puts almonds next to cashews among the foods to swap out at usual serves, which is why the portion matters.
A small handful of nuts such as almonds or walnuts is one of Monash's snack ideas.

faq.q: How many almonds can I eat on a low FODMAP diet?
faq.a: Ten almonds is Monash's standard low serve. Newer data reported by dietitians suggests about 20 is still low; past that, GOS climbs.

faq.q: Is almond milk low FODMAP?
faq.a: Yes. Monash lists almond milk among its low FODMAP dairy alternatives.

name: peanuts
answer: Yes. Monash lists 32 peanuts (28 g) as a low FODMAP serve, and dietitian sites report that its current data sets no upper limit. Both Monash and FODMAP Friendly put peanuts with the low FODMAP nuts.

servings.note: No upper limit is currently published; the bar shows Monash's standard serve.

disagreements.text: George Eats reports that FODMAP Friendly rates peanuts low up to 600 g, far more than anyone eats at once.

notes.text: Monash and FODMAP Friendly both list peanuts with the low FODMAP nuts.
Monash names GOS and fructans as the main FODMAPs in nuts in general.

faq.q: Are salted or roasted peanuts low FODMAP?
faq.a: The published serve is for plain peanuts. Seasoned mixes can contain onion or garlic powder, so check the label.

name: cashews
answer: Mostly no. Monash and FODMAP Friendly both list cashews as high FODMAP. Dietitians reporting Monash data say only about 2 cashews (3 g) stay low, and 30 g is high in GOS and fructans. Activated cashews fare better, at about 10 nuts (16 g).

servings.note: From dietitian sites reporting Monash's lab results; not on Monash's or FODMAP Friendly's own sites.
From dietitian sites reporting Monash's lab results; not on Monash's or FODMAP Friendly's own sites.

disagreements.text: Karlijn's Kitchen (2024) gives 15 g for activated cashews, close to the 16 g above.

notes.text: Monash and FODMAP Friendly both put cashews in their high FODMAP nut lists.
Monash named cashews and pistachios as high-GOS foods in its 2017 enzyme study post.
Monash notes that processing such as activating nuts can lower their FODMAP content.

faq.q: Is cashew butter or cashew milk low FODMAP?
faq.a: The sources we use don't publish a low serve for either. Cashews themselves are high, so go carefully with both until there is data.

name: walnuts
answer: Yes. Monash lists 10 walnut halves (30 g) as a low FODMAP serve. Dietitian sites report that Monash's newer data turns moderate in GOS just above that, at 31 g, so stay close to 30 g per sitting.

servings.note: The moderate amount comes from George Eats, reporting Monash's current data.

changes.text: George Eats reports that Monash's current walnut limits are much lower than the ones its app listed before.

disagreements.text: Karlijn's Kitchen (Feb 2024), using the older data, listed walnuts as low up to 100 g.
A Little Bit Yummy counts the low serve as 15 halves rather than 10; nut size varies, so grams are the safer guide.

notes.text: Monash and FODMAP Friendly both list walnuts with the low FODMAP nuts.

faq.q: Can I put walnuts in banana bread?
faq.a: Yes, as long as each slice holds well under a 30 g serve of walnuts. Divide the recipe's walnuts by the slices to check.

name: pistachios
answer: Mostly no. Monash and FODMAP Friendly both list pistachios as high FODMAP. Dietitians reporting Monash data say about 7 pistachios (5 g) is low, GOS turns moderate from 6 g, and 30 g is high in GOS and fructans.

servings.note: From dietitian sites reporting Monash's lab results; not on Monash's or FODMAP Friendly's own sites.

notes.text: Monash and FODMAP Friendly both put pistachios in their high FODMAP nut lists.
Monash named pistachios as a high-GOS food in its 2017 enzyme study post.

faq.q: Is baklava or pistachio ice cream low FODMAP?
faq.a: No lab has tested them. Pistachios turn moderate after just a few nuts, so a dessert heavy in pistachio is likely to add up.

name: pumpkin seeds
answer: Yes. Monash and FODMAP Friendly both list pumpkin seeds (pepitas) as low FODMAP. Dietitians reporting Monash's data say they stay low up to 81 g, with fructans moderate from 82 g, so a sprinkle or a handful fits easily.

servings.note: No gram serve is published on Monash's or FODMAP Friendly's own sites. This is the largest amount still reported low by George Eats from Monash data.

disagreements.text: Karlijn's Kitchen (2024) gives a smaller low amount of 60 g (about 2 oz).

notes.text: Pumpkin seeds appear in the low FODMAP column of Monash's food list and 3-step sheet, and of FODMAP Friendly's list.
Monash's shopping list includes pumpkin seeds among its seeds.

faq.q: Are home-roasted pumpkin seeds with shells the same?
faq.a: Our sources cover pepitas, the green hulled seeds. Whole seeds in the shell weren't covered, so we can't give a number for them.

name: chia seeds
answer: Yes. Monash lists 2 tablespoons (24 g) of chia seeds as a low FODMAP serve, and it's one of the richest fibre sources on its list. Dietitian sites report that fructans turn moderate only from 37 g.

servings.note: The moderate amount comes from George Eats, reporting Monash's current data.

disagreements.text: George Eats reports both black and white chia as low up to 36 g, a little above Monash's standard 24 g serve.

notes.text: Monash's fibre list counts 2 tablespoons of chia as about 8 g of fibre.
Monash's shopping list includes chia among its seeds.

faq.q: Is chia pudding low FODMAP?
faq.a: It can be. Make it with a low FODMAP milk such as lactose-free or almond milk, and keep the chia near 2 tablespoons per bowl.

name: flaxseed
answer: Yes, in a tablespoon. Monash lists 1 tablespoon (15 g) of linseed or flaxseed as a low FODMAP serve. Dietitian sites report that GOS turns moderate from 17 g, so measure it rather than pouring.

servings.note: The moderate amount comes from George Eats, reporting Monash's current data.

disagreements.text: George Eats puts the most that stays low at 16 g, just above Monash's 15 g serve.

notes.text: Monash's fibre list counts 1 tablespoon of flaxseed as about 4 g of fibre.
For plant-based baking, Monash suggests a flax egg: 1 tablespoon of flaxmeal mixed with 1 tablespoon of water.

faq.q: Is ground flaxseed different from whole?
faq.a: The published serve doesn't separate them. Monash's flax egg uses a tablespoon of flaxmeal, the same size as the low serve.

name: sesame seeds
answer: Yes. Monash lists sesame among its low FODMAP seeds, and dietitians reporting its lab data say sesame seeds stay low up to 51 g, with fructans moderate from 52 g. A sprinkle over food is far below that.

servings.note: No gram serve is published on Monash's or FODMAP Friendly's own sites. This is the largest amount still reported low by George Eats from Monash data.

disagreements.text: Karlijn's Kitchen (2024) gives a smaller low amount of 30 g (about 1 oz).

notes.text: Monash's shopping list includes sesame among its seeds.
Monash lists 2 tablespoons (30 g) of unhulled tahini, the paste made from sesame, as a low serve.

faq.q: Is tahini low FODMAP too?
faq.a: Yes. Monash lists 2 tablespoons of unhulled tahini as a low FODMAP serve. Our tahini page has the details.

name: macadamia nuts
answer: Yes. Monash lists 20 macadamias (40 g) as a low FODMAP serve, and both Monash and FODMAP Friendly put them with the low FODMAP nuts. Dietitian sites report that fructans only become moderate at very large amounts.

disagreements.text: George Eats lists Monash's current serve as 30 g, smaller than the 40 g above, but reports moderate fructans only from 328 g.
A Little Bit Yummy counts the low serve as 15 nuts.

notes.text: Monash and FODMAP Friendly both list macadamias with the low FODMAP nuts.
Monash's fibre list counts 20 macadamias as about 3 g of fibre.

faq.q: Is macadamia milk low FODMAP?
faq.a: Monash's Step 1 sheet lists macadamia milk among its low FODMAP dairy alternatives.

name: almond butter
answer: Yes, in a tablespoon. Dietitian sites reporting Monash's lab data list 1 tablespoon (20 g) of almond butter as low FODMAP; just above that it becomes moderate in GOS and fructans. Peanut butter allows a bigger spread.

servings.note: From dietitian sites reporting Monash's lab results; not on Monash's or FODMAP Friendly's own sites.

disagreements.text: George Eats reports a moderate level from 21 g; Karlijn's Kitchen (2024) puts it at 32 g. Both agree on 20 g as low.

notes.text: Whole almonds share the same GOS, so almond butter and almonds in one meal add up.

faq.q: Can I have almond butter on toast?
faq.a: Yes. Keep it to about one level tablespoon and pair it with a low FODMAP bread such as sourdough.

name: almond flour
answer: Yes, in small amounts. Monash lists ¼ cup (24 g) of almond meal as a low FODMAP serve. Dietitian sites report that Monash's newer data stays low to about 33 to 38 g, with GOS moderate from 39 g. In baking, it depends on how much ends up in each slice.

servings.note: The 24 g serve is Monash's own (2021). The moderate amount comes from George Eats, reporting Monash's current data.

changes.text: George Eats reports a larger current low amount for almond meal: 33 g (about ⅓ cup) on its nut list.

disagreements.text: George Eats gives 33 g on its nut list and up to 38 g on its almond page; both say GOS is moderate at 39 g.

notes.text: Monash's figure is for almond meal. We didn't find a separate public figure for fine blanched almond flour.

faq.q: Are almond flour cakes low FODMAP?
faq.a: Only if each slice holds no more than a low serve of almond meal. Divide the recipe's almond meal by the number of slices to check.

name: butter
answer: Yes. Butter is almost all fat with only traces of lactose, and Monash lists it among the dairy foods that are naturally low in lactose. No upper limit has been published, though very fatty meals can unsettle some guts for reasons other than FODMAPs.

servings.note: Only traces of lactose according to the sources; the amount shown is a normal portion, not a limit.

notes.text: Monash's Step 1 sheet lists butter with plain meat, eggs and oils in the low FODMAP column.
Karlijn's Kitchen reports that Monash rates a tablespoon of butter low with no maximum, and flags that a lot of fat can affect gut movement.

faq.q: Is butter lactose-free?
faq.a: Not completely. Churned butter keeps a trace of lactose, but a normal serve holds only tiny amounts.

freeNote.label: Trace lactose
freeNote.line: Only traces of lactose, so normal amounts are low FODMAP.

name: cottage cheese
answer: Yes, in a small serve. Monash rates 36 g of cottage cheese low, with about 0.7 g of lactose. As a fresh cheese it carries more lactose than hard cheeses, and public data doesn't rate larger bowls.

disagreements.text: Karlijn's Kitchen suggests 40 g, based on her own reading of product labels, and finds 60 g holds an average amount of lactose.

notes.text: Monash's Step 1 advice is to swap regular dairy for lactose-free versions where possible.

faq.q: Can I have a bigger bowl of cottage cheese?
faq.a: Public lab data only covers a small serve. For a larger bowl, a lactose-free cottage cheese avoids the question.

name: Greek yogurt
answer: It depends on whose test. FODMAP Friendly passed 200 g of Greek yoghurt as low FODMAP. Dietitians reporting Monash's data give a far smaller low serve for regular-fat Greek yoghurt: 23 g, with moderate lactose from 93 g. Lactose-free Greek yoghurt sidesteps the question.

servings.note: FODMAP Friendly's tested amount. Monash-based figures are much lower; see the next bar.
From dietitian sites reporting Monash's lab results; not on Monash's or FODMAP Friendly's own sites.

disagreements.text: FODMAP Friendly rates 200 g low, while George Eats reports Monash's low serve as 23 g. Brands differ in how much whey is strained off, which may explain part of the gap.

notes.text: Monash's lactose table rates 170 g of natural (unstrained) yoghurt high, at 8.5 g of lactose.
FODMAP Friendly notes that straining and fermentation lower lactose further, and suggests lactose-free yoghurt in phase 1.
George Eats reports that Monash rates lactose-free plain yoghurt low up to 500 g.

faq.q: Is Greek yogurt lower in lactose than regular yogurt?
faq.a: Usually. Straining drains off whey, and FODMAP Friendly says that lowers lactose. How much depends on the brand.

name: mozzarella
answer: Yes. Dietitians reporting Monash's data list 40 g of mozzarella (about ¼ cup) as a low FODMAP serve. It holds a little more lactose than aged hard cheeses, and Monash's older data allowed much bigger amounts.

servings.note: From dietitian sites reporting Monash's lab results; not on Monash's or FODMAP Friendly's own sites.

changes.text: George Eats reports that Monash's app used to rate mozzarella low up to 630 g (about 4 cups), and that some upper limits were removed during an update.

disagreements.text: George Eats reports that FODMAP Friendly rates mozzarella low up to 600 g per person.

notes.text: Karlijn's Kitchen notes that lactose varies between brands and that buffalo mozzarella tends to have less than regular.

faq.q: Is pizza with mozzarella low FODMAP?
faq.a: The cheese can be, at about 40 g. The usual problems are a wheat base and garlic or onion in the sauce.

name: parmesan
answer: Yes. Parmesan is a hard, aged cheese with next to no lactose, and Monash groups hard cheeses with the low FODMAP foods. Karlijn's Kitchen lists 40 g as a serving, far more than a usual grating over pasta.

servings.note: Close to lactose-free according to the sources; the amount shown is a normal portion, not a limit.

notes.text: Monash says hard and ripened cheeses are low in lactose, and some are lactose-free.
Monash's Step 1 advice is to choose aged or hard cheeses because they are naturally low in lactose.

faq.q: Is parmesan lactose-free?
faq.a: Close to it. Karlijn's Kitchen reports 0 g of lactose per 100 g, and Monash says some hard cheeses are lactose-free.

freeNote.label: Trace lactose
freeNote.line: Only traces of lactose, so normal amounts are low FODMAP.

name: cheddar
answer: Yes. Monash rates 40 g of cheddar (about 2 slices) low, with just 0.04 g of lactose. Aged hard cheeses keep almost none of their lactose; processed cheese slices are a different product and can hold more.

notes.text: Karlijn's Kitchen warns that processed cheddar slices can be high in lactose, unlike block cheddar.
Hard cheeses sit in the low FODMAP column of Monash's food list and FODMAP Friendly's list.

faq.q: Is mature cheddar better than mild?
faq.a: Both count as hard cheeses, which Monash lists as low in lactose. The sources don't give separate numbers for mild and mature.

name: cream cheese
answer: Yes, as a thin spread. Monash says cream cheese has a moderate amount of lactose and rated an 80 g serve moderate. Karlijn's Kitchen reports Monash's low serve as 40 g. Lactose-free cream cheese is the easy swap.

servings.note: The low amount is reported by Karlijn's Kitchen; the moderate amount (2 g lactose in 80 g) is from Monash's own blog.

notes.text: Monash's FAQ names cream cheese, ricotta and halloumi as cheeses with moderate lactose.

faq.q: How much cream cheese on a bagel is low FODMAP?
faq.a: About 40 g is the reported low serve, a generous spread. The bagel matters too: most are wheat, which has its own limit.

name: sour cream
answer: Not clear for small spoonfuls: we found no public low serve we could verify. Monash's lactose data rates 125 ml of sour cream moderate, and a dietitian site rates ¼ cup (63 g) moderate too. Lactose-free sour cream is the simpler choice.

estimateAnswer.line: A ¼ cup is already moderate in lactose. No public low serve has been published for a smaller spoon.

servings.note: No public low amount. Estimated from published lactose levels.

notes.text: Monash's 2016 lactose table lists 125 ml of sour cream at about 3.1 g of lactose, a moderate amount.
A Little Bit Yummy lists ¼ cup (63 g) at 1.6 g of lactose and 100 g at 2.5 g, both moderate.
Monash points out that lactose-free sour cream is widely available.

faq.q: Is a spoonful of sour cream on tacos OK?
faq.a: No public lab number covers a small spoonful. A ¼ cup is moderate, so a smaller dollop holds less lactose; lactose-free sour cream removes the doubt.

name: goat cheese
answer: Yes, in a modest serve. Karlijn's Kitchen lists 40 g of soft goat cheese as low FODMAP, with lactose reaching a moderate level only at 250 g. Aged goat cheese has even less lactose, though no lab has tested it.

servings.note: From Karlijn's Kitchen; we couldn't find a figure on Monash's or FODMAP Friendly's own sites.

notes.text: Karlijn's Kitchen measured about 2 g of lactose per 100 g in soft goat cheese and notes it varies by brand.
Monash says matured and ripened cheeses are low in lactose.

faq.q: Is goat cheese better than cow's cheese for lactose?
faq.a: Not automatically. Soft goat cheese still holds some lactose, so the portion matters just as it does for soft cow's-milk cheese.

notes.text: In Monash's table of fermented foods, both milk and kefir are rated high. Fermenting milk into kefir didn't move it into the low group.
A dietitian blog points to kefir with added lactase: the enzyme splits the lactose, which is what makes regular kefir a problem.
Some kefirs are flavoured with fruit, so read the ingredients as well as checking for lactase.

faq.q: Is lactose-free kefir low FODMAP?
faq.a: No public lab serve exists for it. Kefir with added lactase has most of its lactose broken down, so it's the lower-FODMAP choice; start with a small glass.

faq.q: Doesn't fermentation remove the lactose in kefir?
faq.a: Not enough, according to Monash: it rates kefir high, the same as milk.

name: kefir
answer: Usually not, if it's regular milk kefir. Monash lists kefir as high FODMAP, the same rating as the milk it's made from, but publishes no serve size. Lactose is the FODMAP to watch, so kefir made with added lactase is the lower-lactose option.

servings.note: Monash rates kefir high but has not published the serve size it tested, so no gram band is shown.

notes.text: Monash's Step 1 guide and FODMAP Friendly's food list both put lactose-free milk on the low side and regular cow's milk on the high side.
Monash says most people with lactose malabsorption can handle about 12 to 15 g of lactose a day, roughly what's in 250 ml of regular milk.
Lactose-free milk is still dairy. Monash points out that it lets you keep the benefits of dairy while skipping the lactose.

faq.q: Is lactose-free milk dairy-free?
faq.a: No. It's cow's milk with the lactose broken down, so it still contains milk protein. Choose a plant milk if you avoid dairy itself.

faq.q: Can I use lactose-free milk in coffee and cereal?
faq.a: Yes. A cup of lactose-free milk is a low FODMAP serve, which covers a bowl of cereal or several coffees.

name: lactose-free milk
answer: Yes. Lactose-free milk is low FODMAP at 1 cup (250 ml), as reported by dietitian sites citing Monash. Monash and FODMAP Friendly both list it as a low FODMAP swap for regular cow's milk, which is high in lactose.

servings.note: Sources give 250 ml; shown here as grams, counting 1 ml of milk as about 1 g.

disagreements.text: Karlijn's Kitchen gives the low serve as 1 cup or 240 ml, a small rounding difference.
George Eats reports a much larger maximum still-low amount, up to 500 g per person. That is a ceiling, not the standard serve shown above.

notes.text: Monash explains that a milk can be low FODMAP even when its main ingredient isn't, because the drink is mostly liquid. It names almond milk as an example.
Almond milk appears on the low list in Monash's Step 1 guide and in FODMAP Friendly's food list.
Whole almonds turn moderate for GOS from about 25 g, so almond milk is gentler than a handful of nuts.

faq.q: Is sweetened almond milk low FODMAP?
faq.a: The published serve is for almond milk in general. Check the label for high FODMAP sweeteners such as honey or agave before choosing a sweetened one.

faq.q: Is almond milk better than oat milk on a low FODMAP diet?
faq.a: For bigger servings, yes. Almond milk is low at a full cup, while oat milk is low only up to about 104 ml.

name: almond milk
answer: Yes. Almond milk is low FODMAP at 1 cup (250 ml), according to dietitian sites citing Monash testing. Almonds themselves carry GOS, but most almond milk is largely water, so a glass stays low.

servings.note: Source gives 250 ml; shown as grams, counting 1 ml as about 1 g. Monash's public posts don't name the FODMAP group; GOS is the one in almonds.

disagreements.text: Dietitian sites report a moderate rating from about ½ cup: 120 ml (A Little Bit Yummy, Australian oat milk) or 121 g (Karlijn's Kitchen).
A Little Bit Yummy says results differ by country: UK oat milk was reported low at 125 ml in its article, but only 30 ml in the author's later reply to a reader.

notes.text: Monash's Step 1 guide lists oat milk on the high side, at normal glass sizes, even though rolled oats are on the low list.

faq.q: Can I have oat milk in coffee on a low FODMAP diet?
faq.a: A small splash fits: Monash puts the low limit at 104 ml. A large oat latte can go past that.

faq.q: Why is oat milk higher than oats?
faq.a: Oat milk is rated by the glass, and a full 250 ml glass tested high. Rolled oats are rated by a smaller dry serve.

name: oat milk
answer: Only in small amounts. Monash says oat milk is low FODMAP up to 104 ml, under half a cup, and high at 250 ml. That suits a splash in coffee, not a full glass. Fructans and GOS are the FODMAPs that rise as you pour more.

servings.note: Monash gives 104 ml and 250 ml; shown as grams, counting 1 ml as about 1 g. Monash didn't publish where moderate starts.

disagreements.text: Karlijn's Kitchen puts the soy-protein milk limit slightly higher, up to 257 ml.
A Little Bit Yummy says the small low serve for whole or hulled bean soy milk ranges from 2 tablespoons to 60 ml, depending on the country tested.

notes.text: Why the difference: whole soybeans are high in GOS, which dissolves into the milk. Soy protein milk starts with protein extracted from the beans, leaving the GOS behind.
Monash's Step 1 guide and FODMAP Friendly's food list both name soy-protein milk as low and soybean milk as high.

faq.q: How do I know if my soy milk is made from soy protein?
faq.a: Read the ingredients. 'Soy protein' or 'soy protein isolate' points to the low FODMAP kind; 'whole soybeans' or 'soybeans' points to the high-GOS kind.

faq.q: Is soy milk the same as tofu for FODMAPs?
faq.a: No. They're rated separately: firm tofu is low at a standard serve, while whole-bean soy milk is high.

name: soy milk
answer: It depends on how it's made. Soy milk made from soy protein is low FODMAP at 1 cup (250 ml), per dietitian sites citing Monash. Soy milk made from whole soybeans is high in GOS: only about 30 ml is low. The ingredient list tells you which one you have.

servings.form: soy milk made from soy protein
servings.note: Source gives 250 ml; shown as grams, counting 1 ml as about 1 g.

servings.form: soy milk made from whole soybeans
servings.note: Karlijn's Kitchen, citing Monash. Given in ml; shown as grams, counting 1 ml as about 1 g.

servings.form: soy milk made from hulled soybeans
servings.note: Karlijn's Kitchen, citing Monash. Monash's own post only says small serves are low. No upper band published.

disagreements.text: A Little Bit Yummy reports stricter numbers for carton coconut milk: low at 125 ml, moderate at 150 ml and high at 250 ml. Monash's 2024 post rates 250 ml moderate.

notes.text: Monash's older guide also listed carton coconut milk as low only in small serves.

faq.q: Is coconut milk in curry low FODMAP?
faq.a: It can be. Keep your share of canned coconut milk to about ¼ cup and use garlic-infused oil instead of garlic and onion.

faq.q: Is coconut cream low FODMAP?
faq.a: We haven't found a public lab serve for coconut cream, so we don't give a number for it here.

name: coconut milk
answer: Yes, in measured amounts. Monash rates unsweetened carton (UHT) coconut milk low at ¾ cup and moderate at 1 cup (250 ml). Thick canned coconut milk for cooking is stricter: dietitian sites citing Monash give ¼ cup (60 g) as low. Sorbitol is the FODMAP that rises.

servings.note: Monash gives ¾ cup low and 250 ml moderate. The 180 ml for ¾ cup is from Karlijn's Kitchen; shown as grams, counting 1 ml as about 1 g.
Dietitian sites citing Monash; no Monash public post gives these numbers.

notes.text: Monash weighs a regular egg at about 41 g, with roughly 5 g of protein.
The fructans group is shown because onion and garlic are the usual additions to egg dishes, not because eggs contain any.
Eggs are on the low list in both Monash's Step 1 guide and FODMAP Friendly's food list.

faq.q: Are scrambled eggs low FODMAP?
faq.a: Yes, if you scramble them with lactose-free milk or a plant milk like almond milk and leave out onion and garlic.

faq.q: How many eggs can I eat on a low FODMAP diet?
faq.a: Eggs have no FODMAP limit. Any limit you've heard of comes from general health advice, not FODMAPs.

name: eggs
answer: Yes. Plain eggs are naturally low FODMAP: Monash notes a regular egg has only about 0.3 g of carbohydrate in total, and FODMAPs are carbohydrates. The risk comes from what you cook them with, such as onion, garlic or regular milk.

servings.form: eggs, plain (boiled, fried, poached or scrambled)
servings.note: Contains no FODMAPs according to the source; the amount shown is a normal portion, not a limit.

notes.text: Monash says marinated meats can contain garlic, honey or applesauce, and suggests choosing plain meat when shopping or eating out.
FODMAP Friendly lists fresh chicken as low and puts crumbed or battered meats and onion or garlic sauces on the high side.

faq.q: Is rotisserie chicken low FODMAP?
faq.a: Often not: the seasoning usually includes garlic or onion powder. Check the ingredients or ask how it's seasoned.

faq.q: Is chicken stock low FODMAP?
faq.a: Plain chicken is fine, but most stocks are made with onion and garlic. Look for a stock without them.

name: chicken
answer: Yes. Plain chicken is naturally low FODMAP: Monash lists chicken among fresh meats with almost no carbohydrate. Marinades, stuffing, breading and gravy are where garlic, onion, honey and wheat creep in.

servings.note: Contains no FODMAPs according to the source; the amount shown is a normal portion, not a limit.

notes.text: Monash names beef alongside chicken, pork, veal and turkey as meats that are naturally low FODMAP.
FODMAP Friendly lists fresh meat as low, while crumbed meats and gravies made with onion or garlic sit on its high list.

faq.q: Are beef burgers low FODMAP?
faq.a: A plain beef patty is. Bought patties often contain onion, garlic or breadcrumbs, and burger buns are usually wheat.

faq.q: Is beef jerky low FODMAP?
faq.a: Usually not: most jerky marinades use garlic, onion or honey. Read the ingredients.

name: beef
answer: Yes. Plain beef is naturally low FODMAP, as Monash explains: fresh meat holds very little carbohydrate by the time it's sold. Sausages, burgers, rubs and marinades are the parts to check, since they often add garlic, onion or wheat.

servings.note: Contains no FODMAPs according to the source; the amount shown is a normal portion, not a limit.

notes.text: Monash lists tuna, mackerel and salmon as examples of fish that are naturally low FODMAP.
FODMAP Friendly lists fresh fish as low; battered or crumbed fish falls under its high-FODMAP crumbed foods.

faq.q: Is smoked salmon low FODMAP?
faq.a: Salmon itself has no FODMAPs. Some smoked salmon is flavoured with extra seasonings, so check the ingredient list.

faq.q: Is teriyaki salmon low FODMAP?
faq.a: The salmon is, but bottled teriyaki sauces often contain garlic, onion or honey. A homemade glaze lets you control that.

name: salmon
answer: Yes. Plain salmon is naturally low FODMAP: Monash names salmon among fish that contain very little to no carbohydrate. Watch sauces, crumbs and glazes, which can add garlic, onion, honey or wheat.

servings.note: Contains no FODMAPs according to the source; the amount shown is a normal portion, not a limit.

disagreements.text: A Little Bit Yummy describes the silken tofu limit as about 2 tablespoons rather than giving grams.

notes.text: Monash explains the gap with water: fructans and GOS dissolve in water, and pressing firm tofu squeezes much of it out. Unpressed silken tofu keeps it.
Firm tofu is on the low list in Monash's Step 1 guide and FODMAP Friendly's list; silken tofu is on Monash's high list.
Monash suggests mashed extra-firm tofu with turmeric as a stand-in for scrambled eggs.

faq.q: Is extra-firm tofu low FODMAP?
faq.a: No separate lab serve is published for extra-firm. It's pressed even more than firm tofu, so it's usually grouped with firm.

faq.q: Can I use silken tofu in smoothies?
faq.a: Only a little: the published low amount is about 39 g. Firm tofu or lactose-free yogurt are easier swaps.

name: tofu
answer: Firm tofu, yes: 170 g, about 1 cup cubed, is a low FODMAP serve per dietitian sites citing Monash, with fructans turning moderate from 175 g. Silken tofu is much stricter: low only up to about 39 g, with GOS moderate from 46 g.

servings.note: George Eats, citing Monash. Monash's own post says silken tofu is high at a standard serve.

notes.text: Monash says cooking oils are all naturally low FODMAP because they're made up of fatty acids, and suggests small amounts of oils such as extra virgin olive oil.
The fructans group is shown because olive oil is often blended with garlic or onion in dressings, and fructans don't dissolve into oil.

faq.q: Is olive oil dressing low FODMAP?
faq.a: Plain oil and vinegar or lemon juice is. Bought dressings often add garlic, onion or honey, so check the label.

name: olive oil
answer: Yes. Olive oil, like other cooking oils, is naturally low FODMAP because it's made of fat, not carbohydrate. Monash's example low FODMAP meal includes 1 tablespoon (20 g) of olive oil, infused with garlic for flavour.

servings.note: Contains no FODMAPs according to the source; 1 tablespoon (20 g) is the olive oil portion in Monash's example meal, not a limit.

notes.text: Monash calls flavour-infused oils naturally low FODMAP, because the aroma passes into the oil while the fructans stay in the garlic.
At home you can warm whole garlic pieces in oil for a minute or two, then lift them out before cooking. This works for oil-based dishes like stir-fries, not soups, where water draws the fructans out.
Some brands of infused oil carry the Monash logo, which means a product sample was lab tested below Monash's cut-offs.

faq.q: Is garlic oil with garlic pieces in it low FODMAP?
faq.a: No. The pieces themselves are high in fructans. Choose an oil that is clear of garlic bits, or strain it.

faq.q: Can I use garlic-infused oil in soup?
faq.a: Yes, the oil itself is fine in soup. What doesn't work is cooking garlic cloves in the soup and fishing them out, since fructans leach into water.

name: garlic-infused oil
answer: Yes. Garlic-infused oil is low FODMAP: the fructans in garlic dissolve in water but not in fat, so the oil gets the flavour without them. Monash shows 1 tablespoon (20 g) as a green serve in its example meal. Strain out every garlic piece.

servings.note: The serve Monash uses in its example meal. No upper limit has been published.
